Administration

IO Types

📄 Version 1.0 👤 Audience: Technical Support / Installation Team

Data from Inputs (I) on a device can be displayed on the platform as graphs (Analog, CAN Inputs) or states (Digital Inputs — on/off), while Outputs (O) or Cameras can be toggled from the platform, if supported.

To see Input data and toggle Outputs, you first need to create an IO Type for that IO, and add the corresponding IO on the Device. It’s important to know what the IO connection represents and where it is on the device — e.g. to immobilise a vehicle via a Digital Output toggle, and a relay is wired to Output 2, name the IO Type Immobiliser and add it to output_02.
Before you start: confirm the data is being sent to the platform and correct values are seen in telemetry. Your hardware supplier can advise what values are expected from analog/CAN inputs. Digitals will always be a 0 or 1 value.

1. Create an IO Type

IO Types can be created at Vendor or Client level:

LevelBehaviour
Vendor LevelAll Clients below the Vendor automatically get the IO Type — created once rather than repeated per Client.
Client LevelUse when specific IO Types apply to only one or two Clients, keeping them hidden from others.

All IO Types — Creation Steps

1Go to Administration
2Choose the IO Types section under Profiles
3Click the Plus button
4Choose the Type and enter the information as required per the IO Type created

2. IO Type Reference

Analog Inputs

Enter a Name and Unit (shown after the value — a single letter like L for Litres or V for Voltage works well). You can also choose how many data points to average when displaying data on the front end — None uses every data point; 5 samples averages every 5 data points, smoothing the line if values are unstable.

Camera Inputs

Enter a Name for the Camera Input — a suggestion is to use the camera position (e.g. In Cab, External) or number (e.g. Camera 1, 2).

CAN Inputs

CAN data can be either Digital or Analog data (e.g. PTO, fuel levels). Enter a Name and the appropriate Text or Units for the IO being created.

Counter Inputs

Counter Inputs reflect data that ticks up, like an Odometer, Engine Hours, or Fuel Used (check with the manufacturer whether the value is Litres or Gallons). This data can be converted into a Rate, such as fuel consumption or distance driven per hour.

Name the Input and add Units — Litres (standard fuel unit across devices), Mi/KM (per the Client’s distance unit), or H. The Rate Type and Rate Multiplier depend on whether you’re measuring fuel consumption or distance per hour:

Rate Type & ExampleRate Multiplier
Value per Kilometer — l/100km100
Kilometer per Value — km/l1
Value per Mile — gpm1
Miles per Value — mpg1
Value per Hour — km or mi/h1
Hours per Value — h/km or mi1

Digital Inputs & Outputs

Enter a Name and the Active/Inactive Text you would like to appear on the platform on the Asset.

Temperature Inputs

Enter a Name and choose how many data points to average when displaying data on the front end — useful for smoothing the data line.

Value Inputs

Enter a Name and add the lookup information in the format key,value (example use case: DTC code lookups).

3. Add the IO Type to the Device

Once IO Types have been created, they are automatically available to Devices — you then choose which Input/Output needs to be mapped to the IO Type.

Bulk editing: adding IO Types can be done in bulk across many devices at once via Editing Information on Multiple Devices.

Add an IO Type to One Device

1Go to Administration
2Choose the Devices section under Hardware
3Choose the Device you would like to add the IO Type to
4Choose the I/O section on that Device
5Choose the Edit option under the correct Input/Output section

Once the edit option is chosen, select the IO Type you would like to add, then choose the appropriate Input/Output from the drop-down list — in this example, the choices under Analog Inputs for this device appear:

Once the correct Input/Output is chosen, a pop-up box appears (except for Camera and Temperature Inputs) to confirm calibration is correct — see below for each IO Type.

4. Calibration by IO Type

Analog Inputs

Check with your hardware provider whether the data coming to the platform on the Analog Input is in Voltage, Amperage, or the actual value.

The Calibration values act as a multiplier on the raw data. If left as 0, 100 and 0, 100, the multiplier is 1. If the device sends a value that needs multiplying, the Min and Max values per input need to be set based on the calibration.

The calibration calculation follows this formula:

result = (maxValue-minValue)/(maxVolts-minVolts) * (RawValue-minVolts) + minValue
RawValueThe value in the telemetry before the calibration calculation is applied
maxVolts / minVoltsThe calibration values Max Volts and Min Volts
minValue / maxValueThe Min Value and Max Value

In the example below, the incoming data is a percentage requiring no multiplication (multiplier = 1), so Min = 0 and Max = 100 for both inputs:

CAN Inputs

Enter the minimum and maximum values of the item being measured, as per Analog Inputs. If there is a multiplier, add it to the Input — consult the Device Configuration document or your hardware provider to check for CAN-specific multipliers.

Counter Inputs

If there is a multiplier for the value coming from the device, add it to the Input — consult the Device Configuration document or your hardware provider to check for Counter-specific multipliers.

Digital Inputs & Outputs

Confirm whether the Digital is inverted, and in the case of Outputs, whether it is pulsed.
